source.title: Noise Injection as a Probe of Deep Learning Dynamics
source.authors: N. Levi; I. Bloch; M. Freytsis; T. Volansky

record.file_problem: The supplied text appears to contain the full paper, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: Reports training outcomes for noise-injection networks on Fashion-MNIST, a new dataset setting for the training-error behavior in V1.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training outcomes under added noise-injection nodes. It does not test CIFAR, corrupted or random labels, smaller models, or early stopping. The catapult discussion cites prior work and is not a result testing V5.
record.test_reason: The study measures noise-injection dynamics in fully connected Fashion-MNIST MLPs and a scalar linear model. These do not test V1's convolutional-network training claim. Its noise-induced catapult results vary injected-noise strength, without establishing V5's learning-rate conditions relative to the initial linearized model's stability limit.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors propose optimizable noise-injection connections as probes of training dynamics, identify four noise-dependent phases, and relate noise-weight decay to local loss curvature. They present implications for generalization and normalization as future possibilities.
record.recipe_differences: Adds optimizable noise-injection weights and noise nodes to MLPs; uses SGD on FMNIST rather than the claim's CIFAR settings.
record.method_sensitivity: Noise strength changes the outcome across decoupled, decay, catapult and divergent phases; the paper also says phase boundaries vary with nonlinearity, loss, batch size, number of layers, and learning rate.

fits_no_version.finding: A three-hidden-layer ReLU MLP trained on Fashion-MNIST reaches 100% training accuracy with noise-injection connections.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fully connected networks can fit Fashion-MNIST completely under some noise-injection conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: Sufficiently strong injected noise causes training failure in the studied MLPs; bounded activations can instead fail through saturation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training success in networks with optimizable noise-injection connections depends on noise strength and activation function.

fits_no_version.finding: The linear model exhibits noise-induced loss growth followed by recovery as curvature decreases; MSE and cross-entropy MLP experiments exhibit analogous phases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing injected-noise strength at fixed learning rate can produce recoverable catapult dynamics or training failure.

record.problems: The reported experiments use FMNIST rather than CIFAR. The 100% accuracy caption does not identify its noise strength, and the failure statements provide no numeric training-error measurements.
record.rows_left_out: No other claim-relevant results were reported in the supplied text.

untested.parts: Training classification error in sufficiently large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including random or corrupted labels and the stated recipe qualifications.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training degradation with depth and its prevention by identity shortcuts or the specified alternative recipes.
Comparisons of initialization schemes for training speed and trainable depth.
Recovery or divergence at learning rates above the initial linearized stability limit, and full-batch sharpness evolution at the stability threshold.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization, including Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict applies to V1–V6. The related catapult results are the study's own findings, but their resemblance to V5 does not establish its specified learning-rate regime. Empty row_ids identify related findings outside the supplied rows; these are not missing results bearing on a claim version.
